preamble: Across solutions are 11, when it comes to the subsidiary parts of their clues

clue.text: Fuss about the French city in Spain

indicators.note: the word for fuss goes around the French article, so about signals one piece wrapping another

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion
le is the French masculine form of the

explanation.surface: Someone making a fuss about the French in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic walled city in central Spain, south of Madrid.

clue.text: Open to reassessment of grade, which is extraordinary

definitions.meaning: a script that can be marked again

explanation.surface: A mark that may be reviewed is an extraordinary thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole it means noteworthy and striking; split at the hyphen it means capable of being marked a second time.

clue.text: Country baker is unwell, though up and about

indicators.note: the reversed letters go round the word for a baker, so about signals containment
in a down clue up means the word for being unwell is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: someone who ails is unwell
an oven is a thing that bakes, so it can be called a baker

explanation.surface: A national baker is feeling poorly, though still up and about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baker' looks like a person but is the kitchen appliance; 'up' reads the ailing word bottom to top before 'about' wraps it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is a small republic in central Europe, formerly part of Yugoslavia.

clue.text: Beginner's gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Thor, Norse god of thunder, is the god the theme says the across wordplay leaves out

explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says across answers are godforsaken: the wordplay gives AU, and the answer is that with the god THOR added.
explanation.definitionFit: An originator, someone who begins or creates a thing, is its writer or creator in the broad sense.

clue.text: Girl with posh Roman garment going in for hermaphrodite reproduction

indicators.note: the posh letter and the Roman garment are placed inside the girl's name, so going in marks the insertion

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
U stands for upper-class, hence posh
the toga was the robe worn by Roman citizens

explanation.surface: A girl wearing a smart Roman robe goes in for an odd form of breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-fertilisation, in which a flower or organism fertilises itself, is the biological term meant.

clue.text: The smell of America on English boy's name

parts.note: taken as written
odor is the American spelling of odour, a smell

explanation.surface: An American smell hanging around an English lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore is a traditional masculine first name of Greek origin, meaning gift of God.

clue.text: Five turn into shelter with fine prospect of Manchester

parts.note: Bel, the Babylonian god, is the god the theme says the across wordplay leaves out

indicators.note: the number and the turn are placed into the word for shelter, so into marks the insertion

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
V is the Roman numeral five
a U-turn, so U stands for a turn

explanation.surface: Five people turn into a shelter that has a fine view over Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives LEVUE; adding the god BEL makes the answer. Belle Vue was a famous Manchester pleasure ground, and its name is French for fine view.
explanation.definitionFit: Belle vue is French for beautiful view, and it was also the name of a Manchester zoo and amusement park.

clue.text: Life in France (outside the north) can provide liquor

indicators.note: the French word for life is placed outside the letter for north

parts.note: vie is French for life
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Life in France, away from the north, can supply strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' could mean 'excluding the north'; here it says the French word wraps round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A grapevine bears the grapes that wine is made from, so it can provide drink.

clue.text: Stop? No problem

definitions.meaning: the command '...!' tells rowers to stop pulling, or anyone to steady up
something that gives no trouble at all is straightforward

explanation.definitionFit: As a call it tells rowers to stop; as an adjective it means simple and untroubling.

clue.text: Standard for upstarts

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in golf
Venus, Roman goddess of love, is the god the theme says the across wordplay leaves out

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives PAR; VENUS is added to make the answer. 'Standard' reads as a banner, but here it means the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: These are people who have suddenly risen to wealth or status but lack the manners to match, a French borrowing.

clue.text: Desolate, being so far out with knowledge

parts.note: the word god itself is what this theme clue's wordplay leaves out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of so far are put into a different order

parts.note: ken is knowledge or range of understanding, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: Feeling desolate at being so far away while knowing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SOFAR into FORSA. True to its own theme, the wordplay omits a god and the answer restores it at the front. 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A place abandoned and dismal, as if deserted by heaven, is bleak and desolate.

clue.text: All a person needs to heat the house?

definitions.text: All a person needs to heat the house?

indicators.note: the letters of the first three words must be worked over into a new shape, so this phrase signals rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The only thing someone requires to warm their home.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange ALLAPERSON. Read as a whole, the clue describes the answer, with the question mark admitting the claim is optimistic.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooftop panel collecting sunlight can heat water or a home, which is the claim the whole clue makes.

clue.text: Swampy in comparative involvement with Harris and me

indicators.note: the letters of Harris and me are tangled up together, which signals a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting comparatively bogged down in dealings with Harris and the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Boggier, wetter underfoot: the comparative of the adjective for marshy ground.

clue.text: A vehicle gets older due to inappropriate treatments

parts.note: taken as written
a bus is a vehicle
something that ages gets older

explanation.surface: A vehicle wears out because of mistreatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper uses and maltreatments are misuses; this is an old plural for such abuses.

clue.text: Prince as officer

parts.note: Mars, Roman god of war, is the god the theme says the across wordplay leaves out
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's history plays

explanation.surface: A prince serving in an official role.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble, the wordplay leaves out a god, which is restored at the front; Prince Hal is the future Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a high-ranking military officer, or in the US a law officer.

clue.text: Top secret ("… whisper who dares!")

definitions.meaning: the opening line of A. A. Milne's poem Vespers begins with this repeated call for quiet, then 'whisper who dares'

explanation.definitionFit: The repeated call for silence means highly confidential, and it opens Milne's poem about Christopher Robin at prayer.

clue.text: Young child's young animal born after morning

indicators.note: the letter for born is placed after the morning abbreviation

parts.note: Baal, the Canaanite god, is the god the theme says the across wordplay leaves out

explanation.surface: A little one's baby creature arrives in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives AMB; BAAL in front makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery talk for a lamb, named after the sound it makes: what a toddler calls a baby sheep.

clue.text: Don't talk — manage climb in periods

indicators.note: in a down clue climb means the two pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: An order to hush while handling a climb over periods of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb' turns SH plus COPE, read upwards, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras or ages: long stretches of time marked by notable events.

clue.text: Disdainful expression to support one of very small brain

parts.note: pooh is an exclamation of contempt
to bear is to support

explanation.surface: A sniffy remark used to prop up someone of little intellect.
explanation.walkthrough: Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh calls himself a Bear of Very Little Brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The honey-loving bear in A. A. Milne's stories famously calls himself a bear of very little brain.

clue.text: Number of girls that sing and dance

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
Horus, falcon-headed Egyptian god, is the god the theme says the across wordplay leaves out

explanation.surface: A group of performing girls putting on a number.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives just C; HORUS added makes the answer. 'Number' looks like a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The line of singing and dancing performers in a musical show, as in chorus girls.
